newsitem.title: USA: Consumer confidence slips in March from February.
newsitem.headline: Consumer confidence slips in March from February.

text.p: American consumers were only slightly less confident about the economy in March than in February, the Conference Board said Tuesday, as the general economic outlook remained strong.
The private business research group said its index of consumer confidence slipped to 118.5 in March, down from a revised reading of 118.9 in February.

The monthly report was issued as the Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee met in Washington to consider whether to raise short-term interest rates to keep inflation in check. The Fed was expected to raise interest rates for the first time in two years in a bid to keep a step ahead of inflation and to sustain the nation's economic expansion.

The Conference Board said consumers are "more positive about current job prospects than they were in February," as more than 33 percent of the surveyed households said jobs are "plentiful" today, up from 32.5 percent in February.
"Despite some concerns about an economic moderation ahead, consumer confidence continues to run at relatively high levels," said Lynn Franco, associate director of The Consumer Research Centre.
Franco said the message from consumers is that "both business and employment conditions will remain upbeat through the spring and the summer."

The survey found the biggest gains in confidence over the last three months compared with the same period a year ago have been in the Middle Atlantic states. The smallest gains have been in the Mountain states, the Conference Board said.
The present situation component of the index fell slightly, to 144.1 in March from a revised reading of 144.3 in February, but it remains at a 27-year high, the Board said.
At the same time, the group said the expectations component of the March index edged down to 101.4 from a revised 101.9 in February.
